name: tether
line: Check what an agent says it did against the output it did it with.
evidence: Frozen eval, 120 real claim/output pairs: tether recall 1.0, precision 0.776; a regex matched it (1.0 / 0.95).

name: port
line: Install agent infra on your own Cloudflare account. Preview it, keep it, or tear it down.
evidence: Directory and Sign in with Cloudflare are live. The first installable entry, the agent fleet, is being built.

name: marionette
line: Hard ideas you can poke: autoscaling, PID, interlocks, sync. Each page is a tiny neural network wired by hand, with no ifs.
evidence: Every page replays bit for bit from its inputs alone; the tests and the 3-viewport Playwright gate pass on every page.

name: amber
line: Pause code your agent wrote. A script stops at tool() until a human answers, then resumes mid-loop with no replay.
evidence: Kill fuzz: 210 runs, 1,044 injected crashes, 0 wrong outcomes. In production, replay finished an agent-written script on the wrong result; amber did not.

name: accrete
line: Build each npm CLI your agent calls once in a container, check it against the real tool, then run the saved copy in an isolate with no container boot.
evidence: Sealed receipts on 6 workflows: repeat calls 3 to 18 times faster than npx, same output, 0 container-seconds. Only 4 of 17 candidate tools lift; native binaries and eval stay in the container.

name: hand
line: Computer use without pixel guessing. The device lists what can be clicked, Clef picks one with a probability, a writer is called only for new text.
evidence: 30 bench tasks, 3 repeats: relay 30/30 at $0.0016 a task; Opus with screenshots 22.7/30 at $0.029. No unrequested destructive action in any run.

name: teeth
line: Plants small bugs in changed TypeScript files, runs the real tests against each, and reports the share the tests catch.
evidence: Disproven: putting the mutation check in the agent loop; over 34 Haiku 4.5 seats per arm, off passed 25 hidden tests at $17.80, a free placebo nudge 29 at $15.60, and teeth on 31 at $21.09.

name: ghost
line: Before an agent clicks, will the click land? A model that writes the rule beats a model that looks at the page.
evidence: Frozen eval, 193 real Browser Run pages labelled by a real click: one elementFromPoint call F1 0.883 for free; Workers AI llama-4-scout 0.662; SmolVLM-256M on WebGPU 0.349. A rule Fable 5.2 wrote from dev frames only tied the hand-written rule on every holdout page. Gym of 500 generated pages, scored on 5 unseen families: Fable's rule 0.737, the hand-written rule 0.647, Workers AI vision 0.444. It got 1.0 on an unseen mechanism, but missed the pre-registered 0.90 because some pages change after the agent looks.

name: my-ax
line: Your own agent: chats, saved tools, jobs, and your own computers that it can use after you approve them.
evidence: Live for Cloudflare staff (sign-in required). Moved here from the AX account with 192 chats copied exactly; machines update over a WebSocket, with no polling.

name: radar
line: Reads new arXiv papers each day, scores them for agent work, and hands the best to my-ax as tools.
evidence: Live for Cloudflare staff (sign-in required). 537 stored papers and runs moved here; my-ax calls it through radar__top and radar__paper.

name: mcp-trust
line: An MCP gateway that lets an agent write only to the places you named in your own prompt, and call only the provider you named.
evidence: Real Workers AI agent, real KV writes: fence off, 20 to 30% of injected writes landed; fence on, 7 of 7 blocked, 0 of 20 clean tasks blocked, about 3 ms a decision. A lookalike provider won 34 of 50 picks; pinning the named provider let it reach 0 of 50.

name: trees
line: One Intent UI document, six UI trees. A small IAP host built from the spec renders it through HTML and terminal bindings; build a view once from an intent, then every tree reuses it.
evidence: The host passes 28 of 28 IAP v0.1 conformance fixtures, written from the spec and fixtures alone. Two bindings are real (HTML, terminal); the other four trees are CSS skins. The model call is simulated and the data is a recorded tool call. Checked in Chromium at 1280 and 390 px: one model call, then alias replays.
